  • Multiple enrolled faces (e.g. shared workstation allowlist).
  • External monitor / clamshell behavior refinement.
  • Configurable actions beyond lock (blur, dim, hide windows).

docs.title: Edge Cases — No Donuts
docs.text:
A living log of edge cases to validate together. Each has a decision (or OPEN) and a status.

Status: OPEN (needs discussion) · DECIDED (policy set) · IMPLEMENTED (in code + tested)

# Edge case Decision Status Owner EC-01 On a video call (another app holds camera) Try multi-client shared frames; if none, assume PRESENT and don't lock — bounded by maxCallAssumedPresentSeconds (default 30 min). After that many CONTINUOUS busy-no-frames seconds the assume-present window expires and the engine escalates to absence, so a call app left running unattended eventually runs the normal grace→lock path instead of staying unlocked forever. The cap is NOT the wall-clock time-to-lock: once it expires the engine only begins counting absence, so the effective unlock ceiling is maxCallAssumedPresentSeconds + the absence consensus (consecutiveAbsentTicksToLock ticks) + graceSeconds. A genuinely long call with no obtainable frames WILL be locked at the cap — an accepted, bounded fail-open tradeoff (tunable). Any non-busy outcome (real present/absent frame, suspend, unavailable) resets the window — including the production sessionSuspended() lock/unlock path, so a fresh call after an unlock starts a clean window rather than re-escalating on a stale one. See ADR-0003, ND-033. ND-032 (explicit multi-client shared-frame acquisition) is closed as not-needed on macOS: the OS shares the camera across clients, so a busy device normally still delivers frames to our session (→ normal detection); only the busy-no-frames case uses the assume-present fallback above. IMPLEMENTED blart/homer EC-02 Screen already locked / display asleep / session inactive Event-driven SessionStateMonitor (ND-013, ADR-0009) pauses the loop and stops the camera while the screen is locked, the display is asleep, or the session is not on the console; resumes both on unlock/wake. On suspend the app calls PresenceEngine.sessionSuspended(), which resets absence accounting so resume can't false-lock (the in-tick .suspended capture path is a backstop). Resume robustness: our lock mechanism (SACLockScreenImmediate / CGSession -suspend, ADR-0010) does not reliably post com.apple.screenIsUnlocked, so relying only on notifications left the app stuck "locked" after unlock. The monitor therefore also runs a low-frequency safety-net poll (~2s) that re-reads the authoritative CGSession/CGDisplay state and fires on the real transition — a missed lock/unlock event self-heals within ~2s. IMPLEMENTED blart/homer EC-03 Stranger sits down, enrolled user absent Identity (ND-021–024/ND-034, ADR-0012): once the user has enrolled, a detected face is embedded and cosine-matched against the enrolled reference vectors; a face that doesn't clear the threshold returns .strangerOnly → the engine treats it as absence → locks after grace. A non-matching face NEVER counts as present. Before enrollment the app falls back to presence-only (any face = present). Durable fix in progress (ADR-0014, ND-021): the shipping embedder is still Apple VNGenerateImageFeaturePrint — a general (image-similarity, not face-identity) feature print, so a determined look-alike ("Marco") can still false-accept. Phase 1 landed the real fix's scaffolding — a model-agnostic descriptor, a CoreMLFaceEmbedder (FaceNet/VGGFace2, 512-dim), and embedding-versioning that forces re-enrollment on a model swap (no cross-model vector compares). The structural EC-03 guarantee is only restored once that Core ML face model is bundled and its threshold re-tuned (Phase 2, blocked on the model file); until then the caveat stands (lenient/un-tuned separation). IN PROGRESS — enforced after enrollment; general feature print today (look-alikes may pass), Core ML face-identity model landing via ND-021 Phase 2. ND-073: if identity falls back to presence-only (model mismatch/missing model, or enrollment deleted outside the app, detected via a non-secret UserDefaults marker), the app says so loudly: menu header, orange glyph, repeating notification, "Re-enroll (required)" item. Never silent. homer/wiggum/cooper EC-04 User present but looking away / turned head Detection may miss the face briefly; the grace period + consecutive-absent debounce (ND-030, IMPLEMENTED: graceSeconds + consecutiveAbsentTicksToLock) absorbs short gaps. Tune thresholds. Note (ND-017): the menu indicator now flips to .absent ("away") on the FIRST no-face tick (responsive), while the LOCK still waits for the full consensus + grace window. So a brief glance-away can show "away" transiently in the menu without ever locking — the responsive status and the lock decision are decoupled. OPEN cooper/homer EC-05 Poor lighting / backlight / glasses / hat / mask / camera orientation Affects detection + match. Need robust model + threshold; surface "can't see you" status. Orientation: the Vision source orientation defaults to .up (correct for the built-in landscape-upright, now-non-mirrored camera) but is overridable via defaults write com.nodonuts.app visionOrientation <1–8> for atypical/external cameras, applied consistently to detection AND the crop so matching stays valid. Threshold: matchThreshold is tunable via defaults write com.nodonuts.app matchThreshold <0<t<1> (0 and 1.0 are rejected — 0 ≈ fail-open, 1.0 unreachable → lockout); the live match score is logged to help pick a value (ND-024). ND-076 (2026-09-24): the threshold now lives with the model: matchThreshold.<model version> (FaceNet default 0.50, range 0.40–0.90; Vision 0.60, 0.40–0.95). Out-of-range values are rejected, not clamped. The old global matchThreshold key is dropped once at launch. OPEN cooper EC-06 Multiple faces in frame (user + colleague) If the enrolled user matches any face → PRESENT (v1.1: the embedder currently evaluates the largest face; multi-face scan-all is a follow-up). Shoulder-surfing (user present but a stranger also watching) is out of scope for v1. PARTIAL (single/largest face) cooper/homer EC-07 External monitor, lid closed (clamshell) Built-in camera unavailable → capture() returns .unavailable → engine surfaces honest cameraUnavailable status and does NOT lock (no fail-open; this is now real, not masked by a fake recognizer). User isn't locked out when the only camera is gone. A "not protecting" local notification now fires on entry + repeats ~5 min while unavailable, clearing on recovery (ND-045, NotProtectingNotifier). IMPLEMENTED blart/homer/krusty EC-08 Camera permission denied / restricted (MDM) capture() returns .unavailable (denied/restricted or no device); engine surfaces honest cameraUnavailable status and does NOT lock. No silent fail-open. krusty owns the prompt/remediation UX; a "not protecting" local notification fires on entry + repeats ~5 min while unavailable (ND-045). IMPLEMENTED blart/homer/krusty EC-09 No camera at all / camera hardware error Same policy as EC-07/EC-08: .unavailable → cameraUnavailable, do NOT lock (never hard-lock the user out when we can't see). Honest visible status + the ND-045 "not protecting" notification. IMPLEMENTED blart/homer EC-10 Recognition error / model timeout on a tick Conservative HOLD (bounded): a transient .error tick neither advances nor resets the absence consensus — no markAbsent (no lock-storm) and no markPresent (no false-unlock); state + counters left untouched until the next clean reading. The 3-tick absence consensus (consecutiveAbsentTicksToLock) further damps single-frame glitches. The hold is bounded: after maxConsecutiveErrorsBeforeAbsent (default 3) CONSECUTIVE errors the engine escalates — it treats the tick as absence (markAbsent), so a wedged recognizer runs the normal grace→lock path and locks rather than holding unlocked forever (no indefinite fail-open). Any clean reading resets the error streak. DECIDED homer EC-11 User briefly leaves and returns within grace No lock; reset cleanly on re-detect. Note (ND-017): the menu indicator flips to .absent ("away") on the FIRST no-face tick (responsive), but the LOCK waits for the consensus + grace window — so a brief leave-and-return shows "away" transiently in the menu and then clears back to present on re-detect, never locking. New default timing: effective walk-away→lock ≈ consensus (5 × 1s tick) + grace (5s) ≈ 10s. DECIDED homer EC-12 Photo / phone screen held up to spoof Basic anti-spoofing shipped (ND-041): a variance-of-Laplacian texture/liveness score on the face crop (FaceLiveness.swift) flags clearly flat reproductions. CONSERVATIVE by design — only checked on the ENROLLED path AFTER a threshold match, only flags when the score is strictly below a tunable floor (resolvedSpoofTextureFloor, defaults write com.nodonuts.app spoofTextureFloor <n>, default 12.0) → .strangerOnly (locks). The score is measured on the INNER face region (not the padded embedding crop), so a live user against a plain background isn't diluted below the floor; it errs toward LIVE on any ambiguity/extraction failure and never false-locks the real user. ON by default (toggle antiSpoofEnabled); texture compute is skipped entirely when the toggle is off. v1 is NOT hardened: a sharp high-resolution print or a high-DPI screen at the right size can still pass; the floor needs on-device tuning; motion/blink liveness is future work. KNOWN GAP (ND-072): anti-spoofing is currently INACTIVE on the Core ML face-embedder path (ADR-0014) — CoreMLFaceEmbedder returns the .infinity live/unknown sentinel instead of a real texture score, so the gate never trips there; the check only runs on the Vision fallback path. With the Core ML embedder active, a flat photo of the enrolled user is accepted. Tracked as ND-072 (wire the shared texture score into the Core ML path + re-tune the floor for that crop pipeline). PARTIAL wiggum/cooper EC-13 Laptop sleep / wake, lid open/close Handled via SessionStateMonitor (ND-013, ADR-0009): the loop pauses + camera stops on sleep and resumes on wake. On suspend the app calls PresenceEngine.sessionSuspended(), which resets absence accounting, so an absence in progress when the Mac sleeps cannot cause a grace-less false lock on wake — the next absence episode rebuilds the full consensus + grace. DECIDED blart/homer EC-14 Fast user switching / multiple accounts Out of scope for v1. Partial mitigation: SessionStateMonitor suspends the loop + camera when this session is not on the console (kCGSSessionOnConsoleKey == false), so we don't run against the login window or another user's session (ND-013). Full multi-account behavior (per-user enrollment, etc.) remains out of scope. OPEN homer EC-15 App paused by user, then walks away Respect pause; don't lock. Pause is a first-class "enforcement off" reason in the single gate (ADR-0011): pausing stops the loop and turns the camera off (honest "not watching"), and the menu bar shows a paused state. Options: 15 min / 1 hr (auto-resume via timer) / until I resume (indefinite). Pause is in-memory only — a relaunch/reboot comes back protecting (safe default). ND-035. IMPLEMENTED krusty/homer EC-16 Privacy/cover over camera (physical shutter) Expected: a covered lens yields a dark frame → Vision returns no faces → noFace → counts toward the absence consensus → ABSENT → locks after grace; pending on-device verification. (A distinct "covered" status remains a nice-to-have.) Note (ND-017): the menu indicator flips to .absent ("away") on the FIRST no-face (covered) tick (responsive), while the LOCK still waits for the consensus + grace window. New default timing: effective cover→lock ≈ consensus (5 × 1s tick) + grace (5s) ≈ 10s. DECIDED blart/homer EC-17 Presentation / screen sharing without camera Camera not in use but user may step away intentionally → normal lock rules apply. Confirm acceptable. OPEN homer EC-18 Battery / power profile Duty-cycle checks; possibly slow tick on battery to save power. OPEN blart/homer EC-19 Screen-lock request reports success but may not have locked The lock no longer needs Accessibility (ADR-0010, supersedes ADR-0006). It is a layered, no-Accessibility mechanism: (1) SACLockScreenImmediate (resolved at runtime via dlopen/dlsym from login.framework, no link-time dependency), then (2) CGSession -suspend as a public fallback (login window). lock() is async (await locker.lock()) and its verify poll uses Task.sleep, so the presence engine's main actor is never blocked while a lock is pending. lock() confirms via CGSession before returning true: the screen counts as locked if CGSSessionScreenIsLocked is true OR the session is not on the console (kCGSSessionOnConsoleKey == false, how -suspend presents), read defensively (Bool/NSNumber; on-console signal only trusted when the key is present). If neither mechanism achieves a confirmed lock, lock() os_logs a warning and returns false → engine shows honest lockFailed; do NOT fail open, and no stuck fake .suspended. The prior osascript/Ctrl-Cmd-Q path was unreliable (esp. ad-hoc-signed builds) and needed Accessibility — removed. FUS caveat: kCGSSessionOnConsoleKey == false is ambiguous — it can also mean fast-user-switched-away, not password-locked. It's safe as a lock signal here because lock() only runs while ON console (SessionStateMonitor pauses the loop off-console, ND-013 / EC-14), so at verify time off-console reliably means our own CGSession -suspend succeeded. Timing: lock()'s verify poll shares ONE ~3s deadline across both mechanisms (SAC then CGSession use the same budget, not 3s each), and the poll is cancellation-aware (no CPU busy-spin if the task is cancelled). 2026-09-24 (ND-058/ND-074): the CGSession tool is gone on macOS 27. Fallback (2) is now SACSwitchToLoginWindow, from the same login.framework, and gives the same off-console verification. A launch and on-wake self-test resolves both symbols without calling them; if neither resolves, the app shows a persistent "can't lock the screen" warning plus a repeating notification instead of failing silently at the first walk-away. Each lock logs which mechanism confirmed it. Lock-failed retry and alarm (ND-054/ND-079, 2026-09-24): if a lock fails while the user is still away, the engine retries with backoff (10s → 20s → 40s → 60s, then every 60s) until the lock succeeds or the user returns. Each failure posts a nd.lockFailed notification with sound, and the menu shows "couldn't lock (retrying)". A manual "Lock now" still in flight at grace expiry no longer uses up the auto attempt (ND-079). DECIDED (verified) wiggum/homer

| EC-20 | On a user-trusted Wi-Fi network (e.g. home) | Don't enforce while connected to a network the user has explicitly marked trusted (ND-036, ADR-0011). Trusted-network is a first-class "enforcement off" reason in the single gate: it stops the loop and turns the camera off, and the menu bar shows a distinct "paused (trusted Wi-Fi)" state. The trusted list holds SSIDs, managed via a checkable menu item for the current network, persisted locally (UserDefaults) — never transmitted. Reading the SSID (CoreWLAN) needs Location (when-in-use), requested lazily on first trust; Location is used only to read the SSID (no coordinates). Fail-safe: if the SSID can't be read (Location denied/unavailable, no Wi-Fi), the network is treated as untrusted → enforcement stays ON. Priority: an already-locked/asleep session and an explicit user pause both take precedence over trusted-network in the display state. | IMPLEMENTED | krusty/homer |

| EC-21 | External / virtual camera (DAL device) rejects a fixed capture frame rate | Some cameras — external UVC webcams, Continuity Camera, virtual cams — are exposed as AVCaptureDALDevice, and setting activeVideoMin/MaxFrameDuration on them throws an Objective-C NSException (which Swift cannot try/catch) → the app aborts on launch. Fixed by wrapping the frame-duration set in an ObjC @try/@catch shim (ObjCExceptionCatcher, used by CameraController.ensureConfigured()): if the device rejects the fixed ~1 fps, we log and continue at the device's default rate (non-fatal) rather than crashing. The CMTime is also clamped to the format's [minFrameDuration, maxFrameDuration] defensively. Duty-cycle/power tuning of the fallback rate stays tracked in ND-042. | IMPLEMENTED | blart |

| EC-22 | Multi-display: menu-bar icon only shows on the active display | The status-item glyph must be a STATIC image — either a plain template (adaptive, monochrome) or a colored image with the tint baked into the pixels. A runtime-tinted status button (setting button.contentTintColor to a non-nil color) draws only on the currently-active display's menu bar and is NOT replicated to inactive displays' menu bars, so on a multi-monitor setup the icon appears to vanish (or renders black) everywhere except the active screen — a trust hazard, since the app must always be visible. Fixed in MenuBarController.render(state:) (ND-071): never set a non-nil contentTintColor; for tinted states bake the color into a non-template symbol via NSImage.SymbolConfiguration(paletteColors:) (with a lockFocus/.sourceAtop fallback), and leave nil-tint states (starting/away/locked) as plain adaptive templates. Confirmed on-device: colored glyph now renders on every display's menu bar simultaneously. | IMPLEMENTED | krusty |

| EC-23 | Two app instances at once (LaunchAgent + login item, or a manual open -n) | Two copies each ran a camera session, a presence loop and a status item: duplicate glyphs, competing camera clients, duplicate locks. launchd does NOT merge the two launch mechanisms. Fix (ND-083): SingleInstance takes an exclusive flock on ~/Library/Application Support/NoDonuts/instance.lock before any camera or UI setup. A second copy exits 0 (so the LaunchAgent's KeepAlive SuccessfulExit=false doesn't respawn it). The kernel drops the lock on exit or crash, so there is no stale lock. Any other lock-file error → continue (never block protection). Choosing one launcher per install is still open (ND-053/ND-111). | IMPLEMENTED | krusty/gordon |

| EC-24 | Camera stops delivering frames while the session still reports running (external/Continuity camera unplugged, wedged virtual/DAL camera, capture runtime error) | Previously the last cached frame, usually showing the user, was served forever, so the Mac never locked. Fix (ND-055): each frame is stamped with host-clock time. Only frames younger than 3s count, and frames stamped before the last suspend/resume are rejected (ND-084a). A disconnect of the active device or a session runtime error tears the session down, and so does ≥10s with no fresh frame while running (wedged). The next tick reconfigures, and falls back to the built-in camera if needed. Until frames return, the outcome is honest: busy (a call) or cameraUnavailable, with its notification. Interruptions during calls are log-only (ADR-0003). A failed configuration now removes any half-added input/output so retries can succeed (ND-084b). | IMPLEMENTED | blart |

docs.title: How to use this file
docs.text:
• Add a row when a new edge case surfaces. Keep it OPEN until we agree on policy.
  • When decided, write the policy in the Decision column (link an ADR if architectural).
  • When shipped + tested, mark IMPLEMENTED and reference the backlog item.

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: People walk away from unlocked Macs. In an office that means "donut" pranks at best and a real security/compliance exposure at worst (open email, source code, customer data). Manual locking (⌃⌘Q / hot corners) depends on remembering. Time-based auto-lock is either too aggressive (locks while you're reading) or too slow (locks long after you've left).

docs.title: Solution
docs.text: Continuously and locally verify that the enrolled user is physically present via the camera. Lock promptly when they leave; never get in the way while they're there — including during video calls.

docs.title: Target users
docs.text:
• Primary: professionals on managed/unmanaged Macs who handle sensitive data and attend frequent video calls.
  • Secondary: privacy-conscious individuals who want presence-based locking without cloud face recognition.

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
1. Lock within a short, configurable grace period after the user leaves.
  2. Never lock while the enrolled user is present and looking at / near the screen.
  3. Never interrupt an active video call.
  4. 100% on-device recognition — no images or embeddings leave the Mac.
  5. Negligible CPU/battery impact (duty-cycled checks, Neural Engine for ML).
  6. Trivial to enroll, pause, and uninstall.

docs.title: Non-goals (for v1)
docs.text:
• Multi-user / fast-user-switching presence (single enrolled identity first).
  • Mobile, Windows, or Linux.
  • Cloud sync of settings or enrollment data.
  • Liveness/anti-spoofing hardened to a determined attacker (basic measures only — see SECURITY_PRIVACY).
  • Unlocking the Mac via face (we only lock; unlock stays with macOS/Touch ID/password).

docs.title: Functional requirements
docs.text:
• FR1 Enrollment. User captures several reference frames; app stores face embeddings locally (encrypted at rest). Re-enroll and reset supported.
  • FR2 Presence loop. Every N seconds (default ~3–5s, configurable), capture a frame and classify state: PRESENT / ABSENT / UNKNOWN.
  • FR3 Identity match. A detected face must match the enrolled embedding above a threshold to count as PRESENT. A stranger ≠ present.
  • FR4 Grace period. Lock only after the user has been continuously ABSENT for a configurable grace period (default e.g. 20–30s) to absorb brief turn-aways.
  • FR5 Lock. When the grace period elapses, lock the screen using a supported macOS mechanism.
  • FR6 Call awareness. If another app is using the camera, attempt multi-client capture; if frames are unavailable, treat the user as present and do not lock. (See ADR-0003.)
  • FR7 Already-locked / asleep. Do nothing when the screen is already locked, the display is asleep, or the session is inactive.
  • FR8 Menu-bar control. Status indicator, pause (timed + indefinite), enroll/re-enroll, settings, quit.
  • FR9 Auto-start. Optional LaunchAgent that starts the app at login.
  • FR10 Permissions. Graceful handling of camera permission states (not-yet-asked, denied, restricted).

docs.title: Success metrics
docs.text:
• False-lock rate (locks while user present) below an acceptable threshold during a workday.
  • Median time-to-lock after leaving within the configured grace period ± small margin.
  • Zero locks triggered during an active video call in testing.
  • Steady-state CPU well under a defined budget; no measurable battery complaint.

docs.title: Open product questions
docs.text: Tracked in EDGE_CASES.md and the backlog. Examples: behavior with external monitors/closed lid, multiple faces in frame, glasses/hats/lighting, "someone else sat down" (stranger present, user absent), enterprise deployment/MDM.

docs.title: Security & Privacy — No Donuts
docs.text: Privacy is a hard product requirement, not a feature. The whole point of local recognition is that your face never leaves your Mac.

docs.title: No-recording guarantee
docs.text: No Donuts does not record, save, or share any video or images — ever. While the app is running it samples individual camera frames only to answer one question on-device — "is a face in front of the screen right now?" — and each frame is discarded from memory immediately after that check. No frame is written to disk, kept in a buffer beyond the moment of analysis, uploaded, or sent over any network. There is no recording feature, no screenshot, no cloud, and no telemetry of image data. The macOS camera indicator light stays on the entire time the app is monitoring, so camera use is always visible and honest.

docs.title: Privacy principles
docs.text:
1. On-device only. Detection, embedding, and matching run locally (Vision + Core ML). There are no network code paths in the recognition or presence flow.
  2. No raw images persisted. Camera frames live in memory for the duration of a tick and are discarded. We persist embeddings, not photos, wherever possible.
  3. Encrypted at rest. Enrolled face embeddings (not images) are stored in the macOS Keychain (generic-password item, kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly — device-only, never iCloud-synced), so they are encrypted at rest and access-controlled (ADR-0012, ND-023). Identity itself is computed on-device via Apple Vision (VNGenerateImageFeaturePrint) with no bundled third-party model and no network. "Reset enrollment" deletes the Keychain item. The item carries a human-readable label ("No Donuts — your face signature") so the macOS Keychain-access prompt is legible; the enrollment is read once and cached in memory (the per-tick recognizer never re-hits the Keychain), and a one-time in-app explainer sets expectations before the first write. On ad-hoc-signed dev builds macOS still shows a Keychain-access prompt (its code identity isn't stable); a Developer-ID signature (ND-050) removes it for distribution.
  4. No telemetry by default. Any diagnostics are local-only and opt-in.
  5. Least privilege. Only the camera entitlement we need; clear NSCameraUsageDescription explaining why.
  6. Visible, honest camera use. Monitoring uses a persistent low-FPS capture session, so the macOS camera indicator light stays on the whole time No Donuts is watching — there is no hidden or intermittent recording. Captured frames live in memory only and are never written to disk.

docs.title: Threat model
docs.text: Asset Threat Mitigation Unattended unlocked session User walks away; opportunistic snooping / "donuting" Core function: detect absence → lock within grace period Enrolled face data Exfiltration of biometric data Local-only, encrypted at rest, embeddings (not images), no network Spoofing presence Photo/phone held to camera to keep it unlocked Basic anti-spoofing (M4): reject obvious flat/static photo, liveness signals. v1 not hardened against determined attackers. Fail-open Bug/permission issue makes it silently never lock Explicit fail policy + visible status; uncertain states lean conservative. lock() is CGSession-verified — it returns true only once the session actually reports locked, else it surfaces honest .lockFailed (no silent fail-open, EC-19, ADR-0010). Stranger present Someone else sits down while user is gone Non-matching face never counts as PRESENT (EC-03) Enforcement disabled without user intent A bug in pause / trusted-Wi-Fi gating silently stops protecting Gating fails toward enforcing: an unknown/unreadable SSID is never "trusted" (ND-036, EC-20); disabled states are shown honestly in the menu bar and turn the camera light off, so "not watching" is always visible.

docs.title: Explicit non-goals (v1)
docs.text:
• Defeating a determined, prepared spoofing attacker (high-quality 3D mask, etc.).
  • Replacing macOS authentication. We lock only; unlock remains macOS/Touch ID/password. We never authenticate the user into the machine via face.

docs.title: Fail-safe posture
docs.text:
• Default leans secure (lock) under sustained uncertainty, balanced against not annoying the user via grace periods and call-awareness.
  • Camera permission denied/restricted: do not silently pretend to protect. Surface clear status; pick a documented safe default (EC-08).
  • A failed lock is detected and surfaced, never silently treated as "locked". lock() is CGSession-verified: it returns true only once the session actually reports locked (CGSSessionScreenIsLocked, or off-console as CGSession -suspend presents), otherwise the engine shows honest .lockFailed (EC-19, ADR-0010, supersedes ADR-0006).
  • Enforcement is disabled only on explicit signals, and always visibly. The app stops locking only when (a) the session is already locked/asleep, (b) the user paused it, or (c) the current Wi-Fi is on the user's trusted list. All three turn the camera light off and show a distinct menu-bar state. Trusted-Wi-Fi gating fails toward enforcing: if the SSID can't be read (e.g. Location not granted), it is treated as untrusted and protection stays on (ND-036, EC-20, ADR-0011).

docs.title: Permissions & entitlements
docs.text:
• Camera is the primary permission. NSCameraUsageDescription — honest, specific copy. Camera access entitlement; avoid anything broader than required.
  • Location (when-in-use) is optional and only for the trusted-Wi-Fi feature (ND-036, ADR-0011). On modern macOS, reading the current Wi-Fi network name (SSID) via CoreWLAN requires Location authorization. No Donuts requests it lazily — only when you first mark a network as trusted, never at launch — with an honest NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription. It uses Location solely to read the SSID; it does not read, store, or transmit your coordinates. The SSID never leaves your device (it's only compared against your local trusted list in UserDefaults). If Location is denied, the trusted-Wi-Fi feature is simply unavailable (the menu item is disabled) and normal enforcement continues — declining Location never weakens protection.
  • The screen lock requires no Accessibility permission (ADR-0010): the mechanism does not use synthetic keystrokes, so there is no Accessibility permission to request, prompt for, or recover from.
  • The camera permission is requested at first launch. On the very first run — and only while the session is active — the app shows a one-time, plain-language explainer that it uses the Camera to check you're at your Mac and locks the screen when you step away, all on-device with nothing recorded. It then triggers the macOS Camera prompt.
  • Pause state is in-memory only (not persisted); the trusted-Wi-Fi list is stored locally in UserDefaults and never transmitted.
  • Notifications are local only (ND-045). No Donuts requests UserNotifications authorization (at first launch) solely to post a local "not protecting — camera unavailable" alert; these are UNUserNotificationCenter local notifications with no push service, no server, no network, and no entitlement. The notification text is static and contains no personal data.
  • Tuning knobs are local UserDefaults (no network): matchThreshold.<model version> (identity strictness; per-model, values outside the model's safe range are rejected, so a low value can't make any face match — ND-076) and visionOrientation (camera orientation) can be set with defaults write for on-device tuning. The identity match score is logged locally (os_log) as a bare number to help tuning — never an image or embedding.

docs.title: Open items
docs.text:
• Confirm storage mechanism + key management for embeddings (cooper).
  • Decide anti-spoofing scope and which liveness signals are realistic on-device (wiggum/cooper).
  • Document enterprise/MDM permission pre-grant story (gordon).

When a decision changes, don't edit the old ADR's decision — write a new ADR that supersedes it and update the status line of the old one.
